I found the root cause: in `sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py`, the `_handle_closing_keyword` method had an inverted condition for handling `END IF`:

```python
if unified == 'END IF':
    if not (self._block_stack and self._block_stack[-1] == 'IF'):
        self._block_stack.pop()
        return -1
```

This popped the block stack (and decremented the level) whenever the top of the stack was *not* `'IF'` — i.e., exactly backwards from every other closing-keyword handler (`END FOR`, `END WHILE`, `END LOOP`, `END CASE`), which all correctly pop only when the matching block type is on top. This inversion corrupted the block stack tracking for statements containing `IF ... END IF` blocks (nested inside `BEGIN`/`LOOP`/procedure bodies, as in the "issue194 splitting function" and "parse endifloop" regression tests), causing incorrect statement splitting.

I fixed it to match the pattern used by all the other closing-keyword branches:

```python
if unified == 'END IF':
    if self._block_stack and self._block_stack[-1] == 'IF':
        self._block_stack.pop()
        return -1
```

I verified with manual reproductions covering DECLARE/BEGIN/END functions, nested IF inside LOOP inside BEGIN blocks, and multiple statements separated by semicolons — all split correctly (matching statement counts, e.g. 2 statements for two CREATE FUNCTION blocks, 3 statements for SELECT; CREATE PROCEDURE...; SELECT; etc.), with no regressions in previously-passing patterns (parenthesis handling, DECLARE transitioning to BEGIN, transaction BEGIN handling, GO splitting, etc., none of which were touched).

No local `tests/` directory exists in this checkout (only `git` was unavailable to inspect history), so I relied on the CHANGELOG reference to issue194 and manual reconstruction of representative SQL matching the described behaviors to confirm the fix. The change is minimal and symmetric with the other four closing-keyword handlers, strongly indicating it restores the intended behavior.

structured_output.content:
The regression was an inverted condition in `_handle_closing_keyword` in `sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py`: the `END IF` branch popped the block stack when the top was *not* `'IF'` (backwards), unlike every other closing-keyword branch (`END FOR`, `END WHILE`, `END LOOP`, `END CASE`) which correctly pop only when the matching block type is on top. This corrupted block-stack/level tracking for any statement containing `IF ... END IF`, breaking the "issue194 splitting function" and "parse endifloop" splitter behaviors (matching the CHANGELOG's issue194 DECLARE/splitter bug fix history).

Fix applied:
```python
if unified == 'END IF':
    if self._block_stack and self._block_stack[-1] == 'IF':
        self._block_stack.pop()
        return -1
```
(previously used `if not (...)`).

Verified manually with sqlparse.split()/parse() on multiple scripts containing CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE with DECLARE, BEGIN, nested IF/LOOP/FOR blocks, and END IF, followed by additional statements — all split into the correct number of statements, and no other previously-working splitter behaviors (parenthesis nesting, DECLARE→BEGIN transition, transaction BEGIN, GO splitting) were affected since only the single inverted condition was changed.

No local tests/ directory or git history was available in this checkout to run the exact hidden test names, but the fix is a minimal, symmetric correction restoring the exact same pattern used by all four sibling closing-keyword handlers.
